title: external reviewers' reviews are evidence: firstmate reads them, turns their findings into worker briefs, and answers them on GitHub the way the project's conventions say
acceptance: Why. On 2026-09-29 the captain approved a design for running firstmate-workflow on other repositories (reviewed as an artifact, then grilled on an external organisation's repository PR #164): firstmate inspects a repository and asks at most three questions to write FM_HOME/projects/<name>/CONVENTIONS.md; every merge still goes through the captain's intent card, never auto-merge; external reviewers such as that repo's R2D2-im and BB8-im can be the review, with firstmate's own reviewer only a local pre-check; and nothing about watching may depend on firstmate remembering - scripts do it. This task is one of T-137..T-141, run in the order of their depends_on. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-140.json, is committed on this branch.

Read. For a project whose review is external or both, fm reads each named reviewer's reviews, review threads and comments on the task's PR (gh, outside any round) into the evidence store as that reviewer's latest state (APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, COMMENTED) and its open findings, each with its thread and cited lines.

Ready means every named reviewer's latest state is APPROVED with no unresolved CHANGES_REQUESTED; a reviewer whose request was fixed but who has not returned is asked, in its own thread, to re-check - never counted as passed. Required commit statuses (e.g. a Drone status) and any analyser the conventions name count as evidence too.
Findings become briefs: the external findings of a round go into the next worker round's brief (SK-002) and context pack (T-135) with their thread links and cited lines.

Project T-135 authoritative local round records using its comments/local switch; T-140 adds summary, check and threads under project conventions. Answer per the conventions: post: threads replies in each finding's review thread, one per finding, citing the fixing commit, in the thread's language; summary keeps one comment edited in place; check writes a GitHub check run; local writes nothing to GitHub. firstmate's own brief and evidence never go to GitHub unless post: comments. Coverage and the brief/review loop work identically in every mode without fetching a brief or fm verdict from GitHub. Test every non-comment mode and a stale contradictory projection; external named reviewers are separately authenticated inputs, never replacements for local fm provenance.

Tests from recorded payloads: two bots with alternating states, a stale CHANGES_REQUESTED after a fix, each post mode. Evidence: the required GitHub check and the gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate. Workers do not run the suites themselves. Stubs answer as the real tools do (gh's JSON shapes, a GitHub review, a commit status).

External project data lives only under FM_HOME/projects/<name>/{repo,worktrees,CONVENTIONS.md,tasks,design.md,state}. No private specs, worktrees, prompts, pins, evidence, mirrors or recovery data in engine state or its public tree. Private repos are accepted. Unreadable protection is unknown: require captain-confirmed project checks and policy before readiness, never infer permission or reject solely for visibility. Every GitHub operation names the project repository. Preserve self-project default and explicit-name compatibility. Never push to protected base; task-branch force-with-lease requires confirmed project policy and expected old head. Merge method, deletion, land/review/post and stacking follow CONVENTIONS.md, never hardcoded squash/delete.

Evidence: required GitHub checks and commit statuses plus six gates 1,2,4,5,6,7 on the authoritative current PR head; gate 3 is retired. Workers author feature-owned fail-first tests but run no suites. Tests stay at most 1200 lines; shared fixtures in tests/lib/ or tests/e2e/lib/, with literal helper references. Firstmate verifies CI/gates and real acceptance; a structure check cannot prove model compliance. Commit this task spec with implementation.

Before current-head acceptance, synchronize and verify the authoritative GitHub PR head against the local task ref and isolated checkout. Bind required check-runs AND commit statuses, gates, reviewed head/base/patch, reviewer identity/final-answer provenance and merge candidate to that verified SHA. If remote moves or cannot be verified, readiness is stale/unknown; refresh before accepting. Regression: GitHub update-branch moves remote while local ref remains stale; green local gates must not pass remote readiness. Approval carries only when authoritative current patch-id is unchanged and no later rejection supersedes it. Merge candidate binding is enforced at merge time by T-138 (`bin/fm-merge.sh`).

External reviews identify reviewer and reviewed commit, preserve supersession/open threads and authenticated closed-list semantics for fm reviewers. Stale bot approval or unreturned reviewer cannot establish readiness. Advanced integration remains planned after basic pilot.
